To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the audible sound energy signal is a suitable tool for monitoring machining processes; (ii) the audible sound signal is a function of the rotation speed, feed, depth of cut and the type of material; (iii) the audible sound signals generated during milling operations can be classified by means of a NN paradigm.
the sound energy signals obtained from the milling process can be used as a basis to develop a monitoring system for the detection of process failures.
the audible sound energy signal generated in a milling machine is highly dependent on the cutting conditions and that this signal can be successfully used as a sensor for process monitoring purposes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a robust and reliable system for monitoring milling processes based on the audible sound energy signal.
the development of a robust and reliable system for monitoring milling processes based on the analysis of the audible sound energy generated by these processes.
the analysis of the audible sound energy generated during the machining process, with the aim of developing a system to detect and classify different types of faults in the cutting process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed methodology is a very useful tool to analyse the sound generated during the milling process, to filter the machine noise and to extract the relevant features of the sound signal for the development of an effective process monitoring system.
the proposed system is capable of distinguishing between milling operations carried out under different cutting conditions.
the sound energy generated by a milling machine can be used as a reliable sensor for the development of process monitoring systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the present study, a systematic methodology to analyse the cutting parameters has been developed, and the classification of the different audible energy signals obtained during the cutting tests has been carried out.
the audible sound energy signal is a good candidate for monitoring the cutting process.
we have obtained the best classification rates for the different cutting parameters analysed in this work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the particular case of the machining operations analysed, the acoustic emission signal is more sensitive than the audible sound signal to the cutting parameters variations.
the use of the audible energy sound signal for monitoring the milling process is feasible and reliable.
the proposed methodology can be applied to the development of a monitoring system based on the audible sound energy signal for any type of machining process.
